transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer technical support. My name is Toby. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Toby. I'm having a massive headache trying to connect three new smart outdoor security cameras to my S-Net Hub router. The setup app on my phone keeps saying 'unable to connect to 5GHz network, 2.4GHz required'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly look into that wireless camera connectivity issue for you, Sean. Before we examine your router configuration, may I please verify your billing address and your security question answer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 72 Castle Street, Salisbury, SP1 3TG. And the security question answer is my mother's maiden name, Fletcher.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Sean, that verifies your account details. What brand and model of security camera are you installing?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: They are EufyCam Pro wireless cameras. We had a burglary on our street two nights ago, and my wife and I are so terrified that someone is going to break into our home while we sleep that neither of us has slept properly! I need these cameras online today!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am so sorry to hear about the burglary nearby, Sean. Feeling vulnerable in your own home is horrible and stressful, so let us get these cameras connected and working right away so you and your wife have total peace of mind.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you so much Toby, I really appreciate you understanding how urgent this is for us.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So you are having a massive headache trying to connect three new smart outdoor security cameras to your S-Net Hub router because the setup app on your phone keeps saying unable to connect to 5GHz network, 2.4GHz required.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is word for word what I just said. How do we get around that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, third-party internet-of-things devices and home security cameras are strictly outside S-Net's technical remit, so you really ought to phone the Eufy customer support helpline directly instead.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait a minute! The cameras are working fine, it is your S-Net Hub router combining the frequencies that is stopping them from pairing! Why are you trying to pass the buck to Eufy?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I apologize, Sean. Let us keep working together on the router settings right now to resolve this without you needing to call anyone else.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you. Let's fix the router so the cameras can see a dedicated network.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What model of S-Net Hub do you have connected to your master telephone socket?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is the Hub 5 with the matte grey casing and the glowing white light on the front.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Hub 5 features band steering enabled by default, merging both frequencies under a single SSID name, which frequently confuses low-power IoT chipsets.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we split the bands or enable an IoT guest network for them?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. On the Hub 5, the most elegant solution is enabling the dedicated IoT 2.4GHz sub-network, which creates an isolated 2.4GHz frequency specifically for smart devices without slowing down your phones.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds ideal! How do I access that setting?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open a web browser on any computer or tablet connected to your home WiFi and navigate to 192.168.1.1 in the address bar.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typing 192.168.1.1 on my iPad... the S-Net Hub 5 administrative login page has appeared.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Enter the Admin Password printed on the removable plastic card slotted into the base of the router.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pulling out the card... entering password falcon-harbor-48... logged in! I can see the main hub dashboard.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click on the Advanced Settings tab on the top menu navigation, then click on Smart Devices & IoT.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking Advanced Settings... and Smart Devices & IoT. There is a toggle labeled 'Enable Dedicated 2.4GHz IoT SSID'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click the toggle to ON. In the Network Name box, set the name to S-Net-IoT-Home.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Toggling to ON... typing S-Net-IoT-Home into the network name field.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: For the security protocol, select WPA2-PSK AES to ensure full backward compatibility with older IoT radio chipsets.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Selecting WPA2-PSK AES... entering our household WiFi password... and clicking Apply Changes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The router will take approximately thirty seconds to broadcast the new radio beacon across the 2.4GHz band.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The Hub light flashed green and is now solid white again. Let me check the available WiFi networks on my phone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look for S-Net-IoT-Home in your phone's available wireless list.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! S-Net-IoT-Home has appeared with full signal bars.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Temporarily connect your smartphone to S-Net-IoT-Home so the setup application can hand off the credentials to the cameras.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Connecting phone to S-Net-IoT-Home... connected. Opening the Eufy security camera app now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to check on your overall broadband connection, Sean, are all your regular laptops, streaming TVs, and family devices working properly online?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, our normal broadband has been brilliant, Netflix streams in 4K without any buffering.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Splendid. Now proceed with the camera setup in the app: press the Sync button on camera one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pressing Sync on the front driveway camera... the phone screen says 'Discovering device'... connected to S-Net-IoT-Home! The camera chimed and says 'Setup complete'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is fantastic! Now let us repeat the sync for the second and third cameras.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pressing Sync on the back garden camera... chimed and connected! And pressing Sync on the side alley camera... connected! All three cameras are now showing live video feeds on my iPad!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously that confirms the dedicated 2.4GHz IoT channel has successfully resolved the frequency conflict across all three camera units.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The video latency is less than a second, and night vision infrared is crystal clear. I can see the whole driveway and garden gate.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now switch your personal smartphone back to your primary 5GHz home network, S-Net-Home, to ensure maximum download throughput for your phone.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Switching phone back to S-Net-Home... connected. And the camera app still streams smoothly across the local LAN bridge!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because the IoT network sits on the same internal IP subnet bridge, your phones can communicate seamlessly with the cameras without leaving the house.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is so clever and convenient. What a colossal relief for my wife and me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check the motion detection notification alerts in the camera settings to make sure your phone receives immediate push alerts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Walking past the driveway camera right now... my phone just buzzed with a motion alert and snapshot of me walking! It works flawlessly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Everything is operating exactly as intended, Sean.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We will both be able to sleep peacefully tonight knowing our perimeter is monitored.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have documented the Hub 5 dedicated 2.4GHz IoT configuration on your account notes for future reference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Toby, once we got onto the router settings you were immensely helpful.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your broadband or WiFi coverage that I can check for you today, Sean?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that was everything. You sorted out our biggest worry.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You may receive a brief customer satisfaction survey by SMS after this call; we would be very grateful if you could rate our service today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will make sure to complete the survey. Thanks again Toby.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Sean. Have a safe and restful evening, and take care.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, goodbye.
